name: Brew coffee you can adjust
description: Brew a cup of coffee and change one variable so you can say how the taste moved.
l1c: Brew one drink and say whether it tastes too bitter, too weak, or about right.
l1d: You can judge a cup you made.
l2c: Brew again, changing only the amount of coffee or the contact time, and say what changed in the taste.
l2d: You can connect one change to the result.
l3c: Brew a cup for someone else, ask what they notice, and name one change you would still try.
l3d: You can adjust a real cup and mark the remaining gap.
safety: Heat water only in equipment meant for it. Do not repair a pressure vessel.

name: Cook dried beans until tender
description: Turn dried beans into tender beans and notice when they are still hard in the middle.
l1c: Soak or boil dried beans by a method printed on the packet or a recipe you can show, then taste one bean.
l1d: You can finish a batch you can eat.
l2c: Cut or bite a bean from the middle of the pot and say whether the center is still chalky.
l2d: You can tell done from underdone.
l3c: Season the finished beans, keep them hot or cool them, and say how you would tell they should not be eaten later.
l3d: You can serve beans and state the food-safety limit you are not deciding.
safety: Follow the packet on beans that must be boiled. Do not invent a temperature or a medical claim.

name: Season food by tasting
description: Taste food and add salt or acid until the flavor is balanced, without salting from habit.
l1c: Taste a dish before seasoning and say what is missing, using words such as flat or harsh.
l1d: You can taste before you change the food.
l2c: Add a small amount of salt or a sour ingredient, taste again, and say what changed.
l2d: You can make one deliberate adjustment.
l3c: Season a dish for someone else and stop while you can still name one thing you chose not to add.
l3d: You can season to a point and leave a limit visible.
safety: Ask about salt limits before you season for someone else. Do not give dietary advice.

name: Cook vegetables to a chosen texture
description: Cook a vegetable so it is tender, crisp, or browned, and show the difference.
l1c: Cook one vegetable until it matches a texture you named before you started.
l1d: You can hit a texture you chose.
l2c: Cook the same vegetable two ways and point to the difference a diner would feel.
l2d: You can produce two different results on purpose.
l3c: If a piece is underdone or mushy, say what you would do with it next, and do that if it can still be eaten.
l3d: You can respond to a texture you did not want.
safety: Use a stable pan. Do not leave hot oil unattended.

name: Roast a tray of vegetables
description: Roast mixed vegetables so they brown instead of steaming in a crowded pan.
l1c: Cut vegetables to a similar size, roast them, and show a piece with color on the surface.
l1d: You can roast a tray that browns.
l2c: Point to a pale piece and say whether the tray was too full, then roast or rearrange so more surface can brown.
l2d: You can correct steaming.
l3c: Roast two vegetables that cook at different speeds and take the faster one out, or cut it so both finish together.
l3d: You can handle different cooking times.
safety: Use oven gloves. Do not touch a hot tray with a wet cloth.

name: Cook onions until sweet
description: Cook onions slowly until they soften and sweeten, and stop before they burn.
l1c: Cook sliced onions until they turn translucent and taste milder than raw.
l2c: Keep cooking until the onions are golden and taste sweet, and show that they are not black.
l2d: You can sweeten onions without burning them.
l3c: Add the onions to a simple dish and say what they changed compared with using them raw.
l3d: You can use the result, not only make a pan of onions.
safety: Stay with the pan. Add liquid only if the recipe you are using says so.

name: Cook pasta and sauce it
description: Cook pasta to the doneness you want and combine it with a sauce so the pasta is coated.
l1c: Boil pasta, taste a piece, and say whether you want it softer before you drain it.
l1d: You can judge pasta by tasting it.
l2c: Combine the drained pasta with a sauce so a piece is coated rather than sitting in a puddle.
l2d: You can marry pasta and sauce.
l3c: If the dish is dry or watery, change it with pasta water or a thicker spoon of sauce, and show the result.
l3d: You can correct the consistency.
safety: Drain away from your body. Do not leave the pot boiling unattended.

name: Make soup from what you have
description: Make a vegetable soup from ingredients already in the kitchen and say what gives it body.
l1c: Cook vegetables in liquid until they are tender enough to eat as soup.
l1d: You can turn vegetables and liquid into soup.
l2c: Taste and change the salt, the body, or the liquid, then say which change you made.
l2d: You can correct a soup by tasting.
l3c: Serve a bowl and name one ingredient you left out because it would not have helped.
l3d: You can choose what belongs in the bowl.
safety: Cool leftovers promptly. Do not invent a storage time.

name: Plan a week of meals
description: Plan several meals from food you can get, including one meal that uses leftovers.
l1c: Write three meals and the main ingredient each one needs.
l1d: You can name meals before you shop.
l2c: Mark which meal will use food left from another, and which ingredient you still need to buy.
l2d: You can connect meals to each other and to a shop.
l3c: Replace one meal after you learn an ingredient is missing, without abandoning the other meals.
l3d: You can revise a plan when the kitchen changes.
safety: This is planning, not nutrition advice.

name: Shop from a meal plan
description: Buy what a meal plan needs and come home able to say what you skipped.
l1c: Turn a meal plan into a shopping list grouped so you can walk the shop once.
l1d: You can make a list from meals.
l2c: Buy the listed items or write a substitute next to anything you did not find.
l2d: You can shop without losing the plan.
l3c: Show one substitute and say which meal still works because of it.
l3d: You can change a purchase without breaking the meals.
safety: Check allergens on labels if you shop for someone else.

name: Turn leftovers into another meal
description: Use leftover food in a second meal while it still looks and smells as it did when you stored it.
l1c: Point to one stored food and say what meal it can become.
l1d: You can see a second use.
l2c: Make that meal and show the leftover in the new dish.
l2d: You can cook from leftovers.
l3c: Set aside one stored item you will not use, and say the visible reason, such as a change in smell or look.
l3d: You can refuse food you no longer trust.
safety: When you are unsure, throw the food out. Do not taste food to test whether it is safe.

name: Scale a recipe
description: Change a recipe for a different number of eaters and check one quantity by measuring.
l1c: Point to the yield of a recipe and the amount of one ingredient.
l1d: You can see what the recipe makes.
l2c: Rewrite that ingredient for a different number of people and measure it.
l2d: You can scale one quantity.
l3c: Name one step, such as pan size or time, that you would not multiply in the same way, and say why.
l3d: You can tell a quantity from a step that stays put.
safety: Do not scale a canning or fermentation recipe this way.

name: Read a food label for a choice
description: Use a food label to choose between two products for a reason you can point to.
l1c: On one package, point to the ingredient list and the serving the numbers refer to.
l1d: You can find the parts of a label.
l2c: Compare two products on one fact you care about, using the same kind of serving.
l2d: You can compare labels fairly.
l3c: Choose one product and name one fact the label does not tell you.
l3d: You can decide without pretending the label is complete.
safety: This is not medical or allergy advice. Ask the person with the allergy what they avoid.

name: Tie a knot that holds and unties
description: Tie a knot that holds a load you can test, and untie it afterwards.
l1c: Tie a knot you can name around a rail or a ring, and tighten it so it sits flat.
l1d: You can tie one useful knot.
l2c: Pull with a force you can stop, show that the knot stays, and then untie it.
l2d: You can test and release a knot.
l3c: Given two jobs, such as a bundle and a loop that must come undone, tie the knot that fits one of them and say why the other knot would be worse.
l3d: You can match a knot to a job.
safety: Do not use the knot for climbing, lifting people, or overhead loads.

name: Sew a button back on
description: Sew a button so it stays closed through a buttonhole and the thread is finished.
l1c: Sew a button onto scrap or a garment and fasten the thread so it does not pull out.
l2c: Button it through the hole and show that the cloth is not pinched flat under the button.
l2d: You can leave a shank of thread.
l3c: Replace a missing button in line with the others, and say what you checked.
l3d: You can put a button back where it works.
safety: Keep needles away from other people. Stop if the fabric is too rotten to hold.

name: Mend a small seam
description: Close a short split seam by hand so the repair lies flat.
l1c: Sew a short split so the original edges meet and the thread is fastened at both ends.
l2c: Turn the cloth right side out and show that the mend does not leave a twist or an open gap.
l2d: You can make a mend that sits flat.
l3c: Point to a hole or a worn-out area you would not mend this way, and say why.
l3d: You can tell a split seam from damage that needs another repair.
safety: Do not mend a load-bearing strap or a child's car seat.

name: Wash clothes by the label
description: Read a care label and wash a load that matches it.
l1c: Point to the wash temperature or cycle symbol on a garment and say what you will do.
l1d: You can read a care label.
l2c: Put together only clothes whose labels allow the same wash, and leave one item out on purpose.
l2d: You can sort a load.
l3c: After the wash, show one result, such as a dye bleed or a still-dirty mark, and say what you would change next time.
l3d: You can learn from one wash.
safety: Do not mix a chemical stain remover unless its own label says you may.

name: Hand-wash a delicate garment
description: Wash one delicate garment by hand and dry it in the way the label allows.
l1c: Wash a garment in water with a product meant for hand washing, then rinse until the water runs clear.
l2c: Press or roll the water out and show that you did not twist the cloth out of shape.
l2d: You can dry a delicate item gently.
l3c: Point to a symbol that would stop you hand-washing a different garment, such as dry clean only.
l3d: You can refuse a method the label forbids.
safety: Use a product labeled for the cloth. Keep water off electrical devices.

name: Iron a shirt smooth
description: Iron a shirt so the collar, front, and a sleeve are smooth.
l1c: Iron one part of a shirt until the wrinkles you started with are gone.
l2c: Iron the collar, the front, and a sleeve, and hang the shirt so new creases do not form.
l2d: You can finish a shirt.
l3c: Set the iron from the care label and point to a fabric you would not iron at that setting.
l3d: You can match heat to cloth.
safety: Stand the iron up when you pause. Do not leave it face down.

name: Make a bed so it stays neat
description: Make a bed with the sheet smooth and the covers tucked so they stay when you sit.
l1c: Fit the sheet and smooth the wrinkles you can see.
l1d: You can make a smooth surface.
l2c: Tuck the covers so they stay when you sit on the edge and stand up.
l2d: You can finish a bed that holds.
l3c: Replace the used linen with clean linen and say where the used linen goes next.
l3d: You can change a bed, not only tidy it.
safety: Lift with your legs when you move a mattress. Ask for help with a heavy one.

name: Hang a light frame
description: Hang a light frame so it is level and the hook is in a place that can hold it.
l1c: Mark where the hook must go so the frame will sit at the height you want.
l1d: You can place a mark before you make a hole.
l2c: Fix a hook suited to a light frame, hang the frame, and show it is level.
l2d: You can hang a light frame.
l3c: Point to a heavier object you would not hang this way, and say what you would need to know first.
l3d: You can tell a light frame from a heavy fixing.
safety: Do not drill into a wall if you cannot tell what is behind it. This is not a masonry or electrical job.

name: Pack for a specific trip
description: Pack a bag for a stated trip and show that each item has a reason.
l1c: Write the weather, the length, and one activity, then list what those require.
l1d: You can pack from the trip, not from habit.
l2c: Pack the list and take out one item you cannot tie to the trip.
l2d: You can leave a useless item behind.
l3c: Name one thing still missing that would matter on the first day, and add it or say why you cannot.
l3d: You can check a packed bag against the trip.
safety: Medicines and documents are the traveler's own. Do not pack prohibited items.

name: Read a household bill
description: Read a bill so you can point to the amount due, the period, and one charge you understand.
l1c: On a bill, point to the amount due and the date it refers to.
l1d: You can find what to pay and when.
l2c: Explain one line in ordinary words and point to the meter reading or quantity if it is printed.
l2d: You can read past the total.
l3c: Circle or note one figure you cannot explain, and say who you would ask.
l3d: You can separate a clear charge from an open question.
safety: Do not share the account number in a public note. This is not a dispute letter.

name: Clear a drain with a plunger
description: Use a plunger on a slow drain and stop if the water does not move.
l1c: Seat a plunger over the drain and show that the cup covers the hole.
l2c: Plunge until the water flows, or stop after a short try and say that it did not.
l2d: You can tell success from no change.
l3c: Name one sign that ends this method, such as water rising elsewhere or a drain you do not know.
l3d: You can stop before making a larger mess.
safety: Do not use a chemical opener in this skill. Do not open pipes.

name: Empty a dryer lint filter
description: Clean a dryer lint filter before a cycle and say why the lint should not stay there.
l1c: Remove the lint filter and show the lint that was on it.
l1d: You can find and clear the filter.
l2c: Seat the filter the way the machine expects and start only if it sits flat.
l2d: You can replace the filter.
l3n: Notice a machine you will not open
l3c: Point to a panel you are not opening, and say the filter skill stops at the screen you can lift out.
l3d: You can tell a filter from a repair.
safety: Unplug only if the manual tells you to before you reach the filter. Do not open the heating housing.

name: Load a dishwasher so water can reach
description: Load dishes so the spray is not blocked and a glass is not resting on its side.
l1c: Load a rack so items face the spray and do not nest inside each other.
l1d: You can load for water, not only for space.
l2c: Place a plastic or light item where the maker says it may go, or leave it out and say why.
l2d: You can keep a wrong item out.
l3c: After a cycle, point to one item that came out dirty and say what blocked it.
l3d: You can learn from a missed dish.
safety: Knives point down. Do not wash an item the label says is not dishwasher safe.

name: Descale a kettle as the label says
description: Remove scale from a kettle using only the steps printed on a descaling product.
l1c: Read the product label aloud for the amount and the wait, and show the kettle unplugged or empty of a brew.
l1d: You can follow a label before you start.
l2c: Carry out the printed steps and rinse as the label says.
l2d: You can finish the printed method.
l3c: Point to one thing you did not do because it was not on the label.
l3d: You can refuse an extra step you were not given.
safety: Use a product meant for kettles. Do not mix it with another cleaner.

name: Plan a week with buffers
description: Put real commitments on a week and leave open time where a slip would otherwise break the next thing.
l1c: Write the commitments you cannot move, with their times.
l1d: You can see the fixed parts of a week.
l2c: Place one task away from a fixed commitment so a delay in the task does not collide with it.
l2d: You can protect a gap.
l3c: When one block slips, move one later task and say what you dropped.
l3d: You can change a plan without pretending nothing moved.
safety: None.

name: Estimate how long work takes
description: Guess how long a task will take, do it, and compare the guess with what happened.
l1c: Before you start a familiar task, write how long you think it will take.
l1d: You can make a guess you can check.
l2c: After the task, write the time it took and the difference from the guess.
l2d: You can face the difference.
l3c: Estimate a second task and say which part of the first result changed your number.
l3d: You can let one result change the next guess.
safety: None.

name: Choose with written reasons
description: Make a choice you can explain from reasons you wrote before you decided.
l1c: Write the decision and two real options.
l2c: Write one reason for and one reason against each option, using facts you can point to.
l2d: You can separate reasons from the wish to be done.
l3c: Choose one option, then write the strongest reason you did not follow.
l3d: You can decide and still see the rejected reason.
safety: This is not a legal, medical, or financial product decision.

name: Split work into next actions
description: Turn a vague task into the next visible action a person could do.
l1c: Write what finished looks like for one personal project.
l1d: You can say what done means.
l2c: Write the next action so someone else could tell when it is complete.
l2d: You can make a next step visible.
l3c: Write three actions in the order they must happen, and mark the one that is blocked.
l3d: You can see sequence and a blocker.
safety: None.

name: Run a short meeting from an agenda
description: Lead a short conversation from an agenda and leave a note of what was decided.
l1c: Write three items and share them before the conversation.
l2c: During the conversation, park one off-topic point and return to the list.
l2d: You can protect the agenda.
l3c: Write what was decided and who does the next action, and check it with one other person.
l3d: You can leave a record people recognize.
safety: Do not record anyone who has not agreed.

name: Keep a list of important documents
description: List important personal documents and where they are, without copying their secret numbers into the list.
l1c: List the documents you would need to find in a hurry, such as identification or a lease.
l2c: Write where each one is kept, without writing the full secret number.
l2d: You can find them from the list.
l3c: Ask someone else to find one item from your list, or do it yourself after a day, and fix a place that was wrong.
l3d: You can check the list against the real place.
safety: Do not put full account numbers or passwords on the list.

name: Protect time for one priority
description: Put one important task on the calendar and do it in that block.
l1c: Name one task that matters this week and a block long enough to start it.
l2c: Work on that task in the block and write the sentence you finished.
l2d: You can use the time for the task you named.
l3c: When something else asks for the block, either keep it or move it to a new time you write down.
l3d: You can treat the priority as a commitment.
safety: None.

name: Review a week and change one thing
description: Look back at a week and change one plan because of what actually happened.
l1c: Write three things that happened and one that did not.
l1d: You can see the week you had.
l2c: For the thing that did not happen, write one cause you can do something about.
l2d: You can find a cause you control.
l3c: Change one item in next week's plan because of that cause.
l3d: You can let the review alter the next plan.
safety: None.

name: Tell a short true story
description: Tell a true story with a start, a change, and an end a listener can retell.
l1c: Tell a true event that includes what changed from the beginning to the end.
l1d: You can shape an event as a story.
l2c: Tell it again in fewer sentences and ask the listener what they still understood.
l2d: You can cut detail and keep the point.
l3c: Say one true part you did not tell, and why you left it out.
l3d: You can choose what a story holds.
safety: Do not tell someone else's private story without permission.

name: Ask a question that gets an answer
description: Ask a question that the other person can answer from what they know.
l1c: Ask one question that does not contain two questions, and wait for the answer.
l1d: You can ask one thing at a time.
l2c: Ask a follow-up that uses a word the person actually said.
l2d: You can build on the answer.
l3c: If the person cannot answer, rewrite the question or stop, and say which you did.
l3d: You can change a question that is not working.
safety: Stop if the person does not want to answer.

name: Summarize what someone said
description: Restate what someone said so they can correct you.
l1c: After someone speaks, say the main point in your own words.
l2c: Ask whether you missed something, and change your summary if they say you did.
l2d: You can accept a correction.
l3c: In the summary, separate what they said happened from what they want to happen next.
l3d: You can tell a report from a request.
safety: Do not summarize a private conversation to someone else.

name: Write steps someone can follow
description: Write steps for a task you can do, and watch another person try them.
l1c: Write the steps of a small task in order, starting from what the person has in front of them.
l1d: You can turn a task into steps.
l2c: Let someone else follow the steps without your extra talk, and note where they stop.
l2d: You can see a gap in the writing.
l3c: Rewrite the step that stopped them and show that the new line answers the stop.
l3d: You can revise instructions from a real attempt.
safety: Do not write steps for electrical, gas, or medical work.

name: Write a specific thank-you
description: Thank someone for a particular thing they did, not only for being kind.
l1c: Write a note that names what the person did.
l1d: You can thank a specific act.
l2c: Add what that act made possible for you.
l2d: You can connect the thanks to a result.
l3c: Send or give the note, and leave out one vague praise you were tempted to add.
l3d: You can send a thanks that stays specific.
safety: Do not include private details the person did not share.

name: Read aloud so a listener can follow
description: Read a short text aloud so a listener can say what it was about.
l1c: Read a paragraph at a pace a listener can follow, without skipping a line.
l2c: Pause at a sentence end and stress the word that carries the point.
l2d: You can show the shape of a sentence.
l3c: Ask the listener what the paragraph decided, and reread the sentence they missed.
l3d: You can repair a missed sentence.
safety: Read only text you are allowed to share.

name: Agree a simple exchange
description: Agree a small trade or split where both people can point to what they give and get.
l1c: Say what you offer and what you want, and ask the other person to say theirs.
l1d: You can put both sides on the table.
l2c: Change one term, such as time or amount, and restate the whole agreement.
l2d: You can revise a term without losing the rest.
l3c: Write the agreement in two sentences both people accept, including what happens if one person cannot do it.
l3d: You can leave a clear bargain.
safety: Do not agree to anything unsafe, illegal, or beyond what you control.

name: Let everyone speak once
description: In a small group, make sure each person speaks once before anyone speaks twice on the decision.
l1c: Ask each person for one comment before you give your own view.
l1d: You can hold your view until others have spoken.
l2c: When someone starts a second turn, ask for a person who has not spoken.
l2d: You can protect a quiet person.
l3c: Say the range of views you heard, including one you do not share.
l3d: You can report the group, not only your side.
safety: Do not force anyone to speak.

name: Decline a request clearly
description: Say no to a request so the other person knows the answer and what, if anything, you can do.
l1c: Decline a real or practice request in one sentence that contains the word no or an equivalent.
l1d: You can give a clear no.
l2c: Add one true reason without a long apology, and stop.
l2d: You can keep a no short.
l3c: If you can do a smaller part, offer that part, or say there is no alternative you can take.
l3d: You can separate a no from a smaller yes.
safety: You do not have to give a reason that puts you at risk.

name: Introduce two people
description: Introduce two people by name and by one true reason they might talk.
l1c: Say both names and check that you pronounced them as they wish.
l2c: Add one true, non-private reason each person is there or what they might talk about.
l2d: You can give the conversation a start.
l3c: Leave the two of them talking, or close the introduction if one person wants to stop.
l3d: You can end your part.
safety: Do not share health, money, or other private facts as the reason.

name: Make notes you can study from
description: Make notes from a source that you can use later without the source in front of you.
l1c: From a short text or talk you may use, write the points in your own words.
l1d: You can take notes that are not a copy.
l2c: Mark one place where your note is incomplete, and fill it from the source.
l2d: You can see a hole in the notes.
l3c: Put the source away, answer a question from the notes, and check one claim you were unsure of.
l3d: You can use the notes as a study tool.
safety: Use only sources you are allowed to keep notes from.

name: Teach a concept back
description: Explain a concept to someone and find the part you cannot yet say.
l1c: Explain one concept without reading, using an example.
l1d: You can say it in your own words.
l2c: Answer one question, or say you do not know, and mark that spot.
l2d: You can find the edge of what you know.
l3c: Check the spot you missed and explain that part again in one clearer sentence.
l3d: You can improve the explanation after a miss.
safety: Do not teach a medical or legal rule you have not checked.

name: Work one focus block
description: Work on one task for a block you chose, and record what pulled you away.
l1c: Write the task and the end time before you start.
l2c: Work until the end time, and write down each interruption instead of following it.
l2d: You can notice a distraction without switching.
l3c: From the list of interruptions, change one thing in the room or the device before the next block.
l3d: You can change the setup from evidence.
safety: Stop if you are too tired or unwell to continue. This is not a medical claim about attention.

name: Remember a list along a route
description: Place a short list of items along a route you know, and recall them in order.
l1c: Choose a route you can picture and place each item of a short list at one spot.
l1d: You can attach items to places.
l2c: Walk the route in your mind and say the items in order without looking.
l2d: You can recall the list.
l3c: Check against the list, name the item you missed, and change the picture you used for it.
l3d: You can repair one weak link.
safety: Use this for ordinary lists, not for passwords or safety procedures.

name: Write a journal entry
description: Write an entry that records what happened and one thing you noticed.
l1c: Write what happened, where, and when, in a few sentences.
l2c: Add one sensory detail or one thought you had at the time, and mark which it is.
l2d: You can separate the event from a notice.
l3c: End with a question you still have, rather than a moral.
l3d: You can keep an entry open.
safety: You choose what to keep private.

name: Write a short scene
description: Write a scene in which a character wants something and the situation changes.
l1c: Write a scene that shows what a character wants.
l1d: You can put a want on the page.
l2c: Add a turn so the character does not end where they started.
l2d: You can change a scene.
l3c: Remove one sentence that explains the feeling instead of showing it, and say what the scene still shows.
l3d: You can prefer a shown action.
safety: Fiction is not a claim about a real person.

name: Write a caption that matches
description: Write a caption that says what a picture shows and what it does not.
l1c: Write one sentence that a viewer could check against the picture.
l1d: You can caption what is there.
l2c: Add a second sentence of context you actually know, and mark it as context.
l2d: You can separate the picture from the story.
l3c: Delete one claim you cannot see or source, and leave the caption without it.
l3d: You can keep a caption honest.
safety: Do not name a private person who did not agree.

name: Document a process
description: Document a process with ordered steps and a picture or sketch of the tricky part.
l1c: Write the steps of a process you just did, in the order you did them.
l2c: Add a photo or sketch of the step that is hard to say in words.
l2d: You can show what words miss.
l3c: Follow the document from the start, or have someone else do so, and fix one wrong order.
l3d: You can correct the record against a trial.
safety: Do not document a dangerous procedure as if it were safe.

name: Write a review with evidence
description: Review a book, place, or tool by tying each judgement to something you can point to.
l1c: Write who the thing is for and one judgement.
l1d: You can make a clear claim.
l2c: Under the judgement, cite a scene, a feature, or a quote you can find again.
l2d: You can support a review.
l3c: Name one kind of reader or user for whom your judgement may not hold.
l3d: You can limit a review.
safety: Do not invent a quote.

name: Write a group update
description: Tell a group what changed, what you need, and what you are not asking.
l1c: Write three sentences: what changed, what happens next, and who it is for.
l2c: Add one request with a time, or say that you need nothing.
l2d: You can make the ask visible.
l3c: Remove a sentence that does not help the reader act or understand.
l3d: You can keep an update short.
safety: Do not include private information the whole group should not have.

name: Keep a decision log
description: Record a decision, the reason, and the result you will look at later.
l1c: Write the decision, the date, and the reason in one place.
l2c: Write what you will look at later to see whether it worked.
l2d: You can define a later check.
l3c: When the time comes, write what happened and whether you would decide the same way.
l3d: You can revisit a decision with the result.
safety: None.

name: Estimate, then measure
description: Estimate a length, weight, or count, then measure it and say how far you were.
l1c: Write an estimate of a length, a weight, or a count before you measure.
l1d: You can guess with a number.
l2c: Measure with a tool and write the difference from the estimate.
l2d: You can compare guess and measure.
l3c: Estimate a second, similar thing and say what you changed because of the first difference.
l3d: You can learn from one miss.
safety: Do not estimate a medicine dose.

name: Check a receipt
description: Check a receipt against what you bought and the prices you were shown.
l1c: Match each line on a receipt to an item you bought, and mark a line you cannot match.
l1d: You can read a receipt against a basket.
l2c: Add the lines or use the printed sum and the tax, and say whether the total matches.
l2d: You can check the arithmetic you were given.
l3c: If something is wrong, say what you would ask the seller to change, or say the receipt matches.
l3d: You can turn a check into a next step.
safety: Keep payment details off any note you show other people.

name: Read a percentage in a claim
description: Turn a percentage in a real claim into a count you can picture.
l1c: Point to the percentage and say what group it is a part of.
l1d: You can see that a percentage needs a base.
l2c: Turn the percentage into a count out of 10 or 100, and show the arithmetic.
l2d: You can translate a percentage.
l3c: Name one fact the claim still needs, such as how many people were counted.
l3d: You can limit what the percentage proves.
safety: This is not a statistics certificate.

name: Convert a unit and check
description: Convert a measure from one unit to another and check the result a second way.
l1c: Convert a length, a mass, or a temperature with a factor you can show.
l2c: Check the result by reversing the conversion or by a second source, and show that it agrees.
l2d: You can catch a conversion error.
l3c: Use the converted number in a real choice, such as whether an object fits, and say what would change the choice.
l3d: You can act on a conversion.
safety: Do not convert a medicine dose.

name: Read a published chart
description: Read a chart well enough to say what it compares and what it does not show.
l1c: Say what the chart measures and what each axis or category is.
l1d: You can read the frame of a chart.
l2c: Make one comparison the chart supports, and point to the marks you used.
l2d: You can take a claim from the chart.
l3c: Say one conclusion a reader might draw that the chart does not actually show.
l3d: You can stop a chart from being overread.
safety: None.

name: Split a shared cost
description: Split a shared bill in a way the group can check.
l1c: Write who owes what for a shared cost, including a tip or a tax if there is one.
l2c: Show that the shares add back to the total.
l2d: You can prove the split.
l3c: Change one person's share for a reason the group can see, and show the new sum.
l3d: You can make an uneven split that still adds up.
safety: Agree the rule before you collect money.

name: Compare unit prices
description: Compare two products by the price per unit, not by the package size alone.
l1c: On two packages, point to the price and the amount.
l1d: You can see price and amount.
l2c: Work out the price for the same unit on both, and show the arithmetic.
l2d: You can compare like with like.
l3c: Choose one and name a reason other than unit price, such as an ingredient you need to avoid.
l3d: You can use unit price without ignoring everything else.
safety: This is not a loan comparison.

name: Organize files so you can find them
description: Put files where a later search by name or folder finds the one you need.
l1c: Rename one file so the name says what it is and when it is from.
l1d: You can name a file for a future you.
l2c: Put it in a folder whose name matches the name, and find it again without browsing at random.
l2d: You can retrieve a file on purpose.
l3c: The next day, find the file from the name or the folder, and fix the name if you could not.
l3d: You can test an organization after you have forgotten the path.
safety: Do not rename a file an application still needs under the old name.

name: Write a spreadsheet formula
description: Write a formula that answers a question, and check it against a hand calculation.
l1c: Write a formula that adds or averages cells you can point to.
l1d: You can make the sheet calculate.
l2c: Calculate the same result by hand or with a calculator and show that it matches.
l2d: You can verify a formula.
l3c: Change one input and say whether the result moved as you expected.
l3d: You can see that a formula depends on its inputs.
safety: Do not put passwords in the sheet.

name: Check an automated answer
description: Ask a software tool a question and check the answer against a source you can open.
l1c: Ask for a fact you can check, and save the answer.
l1d: You can get an answer to compare.
l2c: Open a source you trust and mark one part of the answer that matches and one that you cannot find.
l2d: You can test an answer.
l3c: Rewrite only the part you could source, and leave out the rest.
l3d: You can keep the checked part.
safety: Do not ask for medical, legal, or dangerous instructions. Do not present the tool's answer as your source.

name: Recognize a suspicious message
description: Spot signs that a message is trying to rush you into clicking or paying, and stop.
l1c: In a sample message, point to the ask and to one sign of pressure or a strange sender.
l2c: Say how you would reach the organization by an address you already know, without using the link in the message.
l2d: You can choose a path that is not the message's link.
l3c: Say whether you would open it, delete it, or ask someone, and the reason.
l3d: You can make a cautious decision.
safety: Do not click the link, open the attachment, or pay. Do not forward the message as if it were safe.

name: Review privacy settings you can see
description: Look at the privacy settings an account shows you and change one you understand.
l1c: Open the privacy or sharing page of an account you control and name one setting.
l2c: Change one setting and say what other people can no longer see, in the words the page uses.
l2d: You can change a setting you understand.
l3c: Point to a setting you will not change because you do not know what it does.
l3d: You can refuse a switch you do not understand.
safety: This is not legal advice. Use only an account you are allowed to change.

name: Turn on a second sign-in check
description: Add a second check to an account and show that sign-in now asks for it.
l1c: Find the second-check setting on an account you control.
l2c: Turn it on by the service's own steps and sign out.
l2d: You can enable the check.
l3c: Sign in again and show that the service asks for the second check, or show the confirmation screen.
l3d: You can verify that the check is active.
safety: Keep the recovery method the service gives you. Do not share the codes.

name: Take a photo with a clear subject
description: Take a photo in which a viewer can tell what the subject is.
l1c: Take a photo and say what the subject is before you show it.
l1d: You can decide the subject first.
l2c: Move yourself or the subject so the background does not compete, and show the new frame.
l2d: You can simplify a frame.
l3c: Name one fault in the first photo, retake it, and show that the fault is smaller.
l3d: You can improve a photo on purpose.
safety: Ask before you photograph a person. Do not photograph where it is forbidden.

name: Crop a photo without changing the event
description: Crop a photo to strengthen the subject without removing a fact that changes the story.
l1c: Crop a photo so the subject is easier to see, and keep a copy of the original.
l1d: You can crop and keep the original.
l2c: Say what left the frame and whether the event is still the same.
l2d: You can account for the crop.
l3c: Show a crop you will not use because it hides a person or an object that matters, and say why.
l3d: You can reject a dishonest frame.
safety: Do not present a cropped photo as the uncropped original.

name: Film a short stable clip
description: Film a short clip with a start and an end, held steady enough to watch.
l1c: Film a few seconds of one subject without walking, and watch it back.
l2n: Give it a start and end
l2c: Film a clip that begins before the action and ends after it.
l2d: You can frame an action in time.
l3c: Shoot again if the first is unwatchable, keep the better take, and say why.
l3d: You can choose a take.
safety: Do not film people who have not agreed. Do not film while driving.

name: Trim a short video
description: Cut a clip so it starts and ends on the action, and leave the unused ends out.
l1c: Set a start and an end so the waiting at both ends is gone.
l2c: Play the trim and show that the action you cared about is still there.
l2d: You can cut without losing the point.
l3c: Save the trimmed copy without deleting the original, and say which is which.
l3d: You can keep the original safe.
safety: Use only footage you have the right to edit.

name: Record a voice someone can understand
description: Record speech that a listener can understand on ordinary headphones.
l1c: Record a sentence in a quiet place and play it back.
l2c: If noise or distance gets in the way, move the microphone or the room and record again.
l2d: You can improve a take.
l3c: Play it to someone who was not there and ask them to repeat the sentence.
l3d: You can test the recording on another person.
safety: Record only people who agreed.

name: Follow a shot list
description: Write the shots you need and collect them, including one you had to change.
l1c: Write three shots, each with a subject.
l2c: Take each shot and tick it only if the subject is the one you wrote.
l2d: You can follow the list.
l3c: If one shot is impossible, write a replacement that still serves the same purpose.
l3d: You can adapt a list on the spot.
safety: Do not take risks to get a shot.

name: Keep a steady beat
description: Keep a pulse with your hands while a song or a metronome continues.
l1c: Clap with a metronome or a recording and stay with it for a short passage.
l1d: You can match a pulse you can hear.
l2c: Keep clapping when the click stops for a few beats, then show whether you met it when it returns.
l2d: You can hold a pulse briefly.
l3c: Keep the pulse while someone sings or a melody plays, and stop if you drift, then say where.
l3d: You can support a melody without taking it over.
safety: Keep the volume safe for your ears.

name: Match a pitch
description: Sing or hum a note you just heard, and notice when you are flat or sharp.
l1c: Hear a note and sing or hum it back so a tuner or another person says it matches.
l2c: If you miss, say whether you were low or high, using a tuner or a listener, and try once more.
l2d: You can name the direction of a miss.
l3c: Match three notes in a row and mark the one that was least sure.
l3d: You can carry a short pattern.
safety: Stop if your voice hurts. Do not force a high note.

name: Learn a short tune by ear
description: Learn a short tune by listening, without requiring an instrument.
l1c: Listen to a short tune and sing or hum its shape back.
l2c: Mark the phrase you lose, listen only to that phrase, and sing it again.
l2d: You can isolate a hard phrase.
l3c: Sing or play the tune from the start without the recording, and name the phrase you still need.
l3d: You can hold a tune from memory and see the gap.
safety: Use music you are allowed to learn from. This is not a performance right.

name: Clap a written rhythm
description: Clap a simple written rhythm and keep the beat under it.
l1c: Clap a short written pattern of long and short notes while you can see it.
l1d: You can read a simple rhythm.
l2c: Tap the pulse with a foot while the hands clap the pattern.
l2d: You can separate pulse and rhythm.
l3c: When you stumble, stop, count that bar, and clap it correctly once.
l3d: You can repair a bar.
safety: None.

name: Draw an object you are looking at
description: Draw an object in front of you, and correct one proportion from a second look.
l1c: Draw the outer shape of an object while you look at it.
l1d: You can record a shape from sight.
l2c: Compare one width or height with the object and change the drawing.
l2d: You can correct a proportion.
l3c: Add one shadow or overlap you missed, and point to it on the object.
l3d: You can add a detail you verified.
safety: Do not draw a person who has not agreed. This is not the sky-sketching skill.

name: Mix a color you can match
description: Mix a paint or a digital color until it is closer to a sample than your first try.
l1c: Mix a color aimed at a sample you can see.
l1d: You can mix toward a target.
l2c: Say whether the mix is too light, too dark, or too far toward one hue, and change only that.
l2d: You can steer a mix.
l3c: Put the mix next to the sample and say what difference remains.
l3d: You can judge a match honestly.
safety: Use paints as their labels say. Do not mix unknown chemicals.

name: Letter a short word by hand
description: Letter a word so the letters share a height and the word can be read.
l1c: Write a word in capitals or a consistent script, slowly enough to control the shapes.
l2c: Draw a guide and remake the word so the letters sit between the lines.
l2d: You can use a guide.
l3c: Adjust one awkward gap and show the word to someone who can read it at a glance.
l3d: You can make a word readable, not only neat.
safety: None.

name: Make a collage with a point
description: Arrange found images so a viewer can say what point the collage makes.
l1c: Write the point in one sentence before you stick anything down.
l1d: You can start from a point.
l2c: Arrange at least three pieces so they support that sentence, and fix them.
l2d: You can build the point from pieces.
l3c: Ask someone what they think the point is, and change or remove one piece if they cannot tell.
l3d: You can revise from a viewer.
safety: Use images you are allowed to reuse. Do not copy a protected picture into a public post as your own.

name: Fold a paper box
description: Fold a box from paper that closes and holds a small object.
l1c: Fold a sheet on a pattern you can show, with creases that meet.
l1d: You can follow a fold pattern.
l2c: Assemble it so a lid or flap closes.
l2d: You can make a closed box.
l3c: Put a small object inside, close it, and reinforce or refold the corner that fails.
l3d: You can make a box that works.
safety: Mind sharp paper edges. This is not a model of a machine.

name: Braid a cord
description: Braid three strands into a cord that stays together at the ends.
l1c: Fasten three strands and braid until the pattern repeats.
l1d: You can keep a three-strand pattern.
l2c: Show a length where the strands are equally tight, and redo a loose bit.
l2d: You can even the tension.
l3c: Stop the end so it does not unravel, and hang a light object from the cord.
l3d: You can finish a cord that holds a small load.
safety: Do not use it to hold a person or a heavy load.

name: Smooth a small piece of wood
description: Sand a small wooden offcut until the surface you chose is smoother than when you started.
l1c: Sand one face and show the difference with a fingertip or a side-by-side look.
l2c: Use a finer grit after a coarser one, and say which scratch the finer grit is removing.
l2d: You can move from coarse to fine.
l3c: Stop before any oil or varnish, and say what you would need to know before adding one.
l3d: You can separate sanding from a chemical finish.
safety: Wear a mask if the dust bothers you. Do not sand unknown painted wood that might contain old lead paint.

name: Glue a clean joint
description: Glue two pieces so the joint holds after it has set, using a glue meant for those materials.
l1c: Fit the pieces without glue and mark their position.
l1d: You can fit before you glue.
l2c: Apply glue as its label says, align the marks, and hold or clamp until the label's set starts.
l2d: You can make a joint.
l3c: After the label's wait, test the joint with a gentle load and say whether it held.
l3d: You can wait and then test.
safety: Use the glue's ventilation warning. Do not glue skin. This is not a structural repair.

name: Wrap a parcel so it stays closed
description: Wrap an object so the paper stays closed when you pick it up.
l1c: Cut paper that covers the object with overlap, and fold the first seam.
l2c: Fold both ends so no open flap hangs out.
l2d: You can close the ends.
l3c: Pick the parcel up by the top and secure any flap that opens.
l3d: You can make a wrap that survives handling.
safety: Keep scissors closed when you put them down.

name: Make a simple notebook
description: Bind a few sheets into a cover so the pages turn and stay in.
l1c: Fold sheets into a section and nest them.
l2c: Fasten the section into a cover so pages do not fall out when you shake it gently.
l2d: You can bind a section.
l3c: Write a line on the first and last page and show that the fastening still holds.
l3d: You can use the notebook you made.
safety: Mind the needle if you sew the spine.

name: Make a small textile square
description: Knit or crochet a small square with an even edge, using one method.
l1c: Cast on or chain, and make one row of stitches you can count.
l2c: Add rows until you have a square, and count the stitches at the end against the start.
l2d: You can keep a stitch count.
l3c: Bind or fasten off, and show an edge that does not unravel when you tug gently.
l3d: You can finish a square.
safety: This is one method, not a separate skill for every craft.

name: Water a plant by checking the soil
description: Decide whether to water a plant by feeling the soil, not by the calendar alone.
l1c: Touch the soil below the surface and say whether it is dry or damp.
l1d: You can check before you water.
l2c: Water only if it is dry, or leave it and say why.
l2d: You can choose to wait.
l3c: Look the next day and say whether the plant or the soil suggests you gave too much or too little.
l3d: You can learn from the next day.
safety: Do not use a pesticide. Empty standing water in a saucer if mosquitoes are a concern where you live.

name: Repot a plant
description: Move a plant into a slightly larger pot without burying the stem deeper than it was.
l1c: Slide the plant out and show whether the roots circle the ball.
l1d: You can inspect the root ball.
l2c: Place it in the new pot at the same stem depth and fill around it.
l2d: You can keep the stem at the right height.
l3c: Water it in, put it where it was growing, and name one sign that would make you ask for advice.
l3d: You can settle a plant and know when to ask.
safety: Lift with care. Do not repot a plant whose label says to leave it. This is not pest diagnosis.

name: Compost kitchen scraps
description: Add kitchen scraps to a compost setup and keep out what does not belong.
l1c: Put an allowed fruit or vegetable scrap into a compost bin or pile you are allowed to use.
l2c: Name one kitchen waste you will not add, and why this setup refuses it.
l2d: You can exclude the wrong waste.
l3c: Look at the pile, say whether it is too wet or too dry to the eye, and add dry material or pause scraps accordingly.
l3d: You can respond to what you see.
safety: Follow the local rule for meat, dairy, and cooked food. Do not treat compost as sterile soil for a wound or for food contact.

name: Name plants you can find nearby
description: Identify a plant near you with a guide, and say what you are still unsure of.
l1c: Match one plant to a guide using a leaf or a flower you can see.
l2c: Confirm or doubt the match with a second feature, such as the leaf edge or the growth habit.
l2d: You can test an identification.
l3c: Point to a plant you will not name, and say which feature is missing.
l3d: You can refuse a guess.
safety: Do not eat a plant because you named it. Identification here is not foraging advice.

name: Save and label a seed
description: Save a seed from food or a plant you grew, and label what it is and when you took it.
l1c: Take seeds from one plant or fruit and dry them so they are not damp to the touch.
l1d: You can prepare a seed to store.
l2c: Write the name and the date on the container.
l2d: You can label what you saved.
l3c: Write whether you know if the seed will grow true, or that you do not know.
l3d: You can store a seed without promising the plant.
safety: Do not save seed treated for eating, such as seed sold to cook, unless you know it is viable and legal to grow.

name: Support a climbing plant
description: Give a climbing plant a support and tie it so the stem is held, not cut.
l1c: Put a stake or a string in place before the stem bends.
l2c: Tie the stem with a loop that does not pinch, and show a finger of room.
l2d: You can tie without strangling the stem.
l3c: Look again after the plant has grown and move or loosen a tie that has become tight.
l3d: You can maintain a tie.
safety: Do not use wire that can cut the stem.

name: Harvest an herb without killing it
description: Take a small harvest from a living herb and leave enough growth for the plant to continue.
l1c: Cut or pinch a small amount from the tips, not the whole plant.
l1d: You can take a small harvest.
l2c: Show the leaves or shoots you left, and say why they are enough.
l2d: You can leave the plant able to grow.
l3c: Use the cut herb the same day or say how you dried a piece, and note the plant's response if you look again.
l3d: You can connect the harvest to use.
safety: Eat only herbs you know are culinary and untreated. This skill is the cut, not plant identification for foraging.

name: Find a rough direction from the sun
description: Use the sun and the time of day to name a rough direction, and say when you would not trust it.
l1c: In daylight, point to the sun and say which horizon it is toward.
l1d: You can relate the sun to the horizon.
l2c: Using the time of day, name one rough cardinal direction and how you got it.
l2d: You can make a rough call.
l3c: Say one condition, such as heavy cloud or being unsure of the time, when you would use a map or ask instead.
l3d: You can refuse a sun bearing when it is weak.
safety: Do not look at the sun. This is not navigation for a wilderness trip.

name: Read a city transit map
description: Use a transit map to name a route between two stops.
l1c: Find your stop and the stop you want on a map or a posted diagram.
l2c: Name the line and the direction, and one place you would change if needed.
l2d: You can read a route.
l3c: If a notice says the line is broken, name another way or say you would ask.
l3d: You can respond to a break in the route.
safety: Stand back from the platform edge while you read.

name: Plan a walk you can return from
description: Plan a short walk with a turn-around time and a way back you can describe.
l1c: On a map, mark a short route and the point where you turn around.
l1d: You can plan a bounded walk.
l2c: Write the time you will turn around even if you have not finished.
l2d: You can put a limit on the walk.
l3c: Say the way back in a sentence someone else could follow, including one landmark.
l3d: You can explain the return.
safety: Tell someone where you are going. This is not remote navigation. Turn back if the weather turns.

name: Read a trail marker
description: Follow a trail marker you can see, and stop when the next marker is missing.
l1c: Point to a blaze, a cairn, or a sign and say what direction it gives.
l2c: Walk only as far as the next marker you can see, and show it.
l2d: You can link two markers.
l3c: If you cannot see the next marker, stop and say how you will go back to the last one.
l3d: You can stop rather than guess.
safety: Do not leave a marked route to search. This is not off-trail navigation.

name: Pitch a tent so it stays up
description: Pitch a tent from its own picture or instructions so the poles are seated and the door closes.
l1c: Lay the tent out and identify the door and the pole sleeves from the instructions or the color codes.
l1d: You can read the tent before you raise it.
l2c: Seat the poles and close the door, and show that the inner is not twisted.
l2d: You can raise a tent.
l3c: Peg or weight the side that lifts, and say what you would do if the wind increased beyond this site.
l3d: You can secure a tent and name a condition that ends the camp.
safety: Use a site where tents are allowed. Do not pitch under a dead branch or in a flood path. Do not use a stove in this skill.

name: Inflate a tire to the marked pressure
description: Inflate a bicycle tire to a pressure written on the tire, and check it.
l1c: Read the pressure range printed on the tire, including the unit.
l1d: You can find the number that matters.
l2c: Add air and check with a gauge, stopping inside the printed range.
l2d: You can hit a printed range.
l3c: If you removed nothing, spin the wheel and say whether it rubs. If it rubs, stop and say you would ask before forcing it.
l3d: You can notice a rub and stop.
safety: Do not exceed the pressure on the tire. Keep your face away from the valve.

name: Mend a bicycle puncture
description: Find a hole in a bicycle inner tube, patch it, and show that it holds air.
l1c: Remove the wheel if you need to, take out the tube, and find the hole with water or by feeling the escaping air.
l2c: Apply a patch kit as its own instructions say, and wait as those instructions say.
l2d: You can patch a tube.
l3c: Refit the tube without pinching it, inflate within the tire's range, and show that it still holds after a few minutes.
l3d: You can return a wheel to a holding tire.
safety: Work off the road. Do not use a knife toward your hand. If the tire wall is split, do not ride it.

name: Braid hair so it holds
description: Braid hair, with permission, so the braid stays for ordinary movement.
l1c: Divide the hair into three sections that start evenly.
l2c: Braid to the end and fasten it so it does not immediately fall apart.
l2d: You can finish a braid.
l3c: Ask whether it pulls, and loosen a start that the person says is too tight.
l3d: You can make a braid comfortable.
safety: Only with the person's permission. Stop if they say it hurts.

name: Tie a necktie or a scarf
description: Tie a necktie or a scarf so it stays and sits in the center.
l1c: Tie a standard knot from a diagram you can show, and tighten it gently.
l2c: Center the knot at the collar and make the ends the length you intended.
l2d: You can adjust the finish.
l3c: Untie it and show that the cloth is not crumpled into a hard knot.
l3d: You can undo the tie.
safety: Do not pull a neckwear tight. Never tie anything around a child's neck as a game.

name: Polish a pair of shoes
description: Clean and polish leather shoes so the dull area you started with looks even.
l1c: Remove dried dirt and let the shoe dry if it was wet.
l2c: Apply a thin coat of polish suited to the shoe and buff one shoe to an even look.
l2d: You can polish one shoe.
l3c: Do the second shoe and say which scuff you did not try to hide because it is damage, not dirt.
l3d: You can finish a pair and leave real damage visible.
safety: Use the polish in a ventilated space. Do not polish a wet shoe with heat.

name: Address an envelope
description: Address an envelope so a postal worker can find the recipient and the return address.
l1c: Write a recipient and an address in the order your postal service shows on its example.
l1d: You can follow an address order.
l2c: Add a return address where it will not be confused with the destination.
l2d: You can include a return path.
l3c: Read it as if you did not know the person, and correct one ambiguity.
l3d: You can catch an unclear address.
safety: Do not write an account number on the outside.

name: Send a package
description: Pack an object and hand it to a counter with the address and the service you chose.
l1c: Pack an object so it does not rattle, and close the box.
l1d: You can pack for a trip through the post.
l2c: At home or at the counter, choose a service and say what the receipt says about delivery.
l2d: You can choose how it will travel.
l3c: Keep the receipt or tracking number, and say where you stored it.
l3d: You can prove you sent it.
safety: Do not send prohibited items. Follow the counter's list.

name: Leave a clear voicemail
description: Leave a voicemail that says who you are, why you called, and how to reply.
l1c: Record a message that starts with your name and one reason for the call.
l2c: Leave a callback number or another reply path, spoken slowly enough to write down.
l2d: You can make a reply possible.
l3c: If the system lets you, listen back and rerecord if your name or number was unclear.
l3d: You can check the message.
safety: Do not leave passwords, medical detail, or payment card numbers.

name: Fill in a form completely
description: Complete a form and check it before you send it.
l1c: Fill each required field, and mark a field you do not understand instead of inventing an answer.
l1d: You can complete what you know.
l2c: Where the form asks for a fact you can check, copy it from the document rather than from memory.
l2d: You can copy a fact carefully.
l3c: Read the form once more, correct one error, and only then send or say you are ready.
l3d: You can review before you submit.
safety: Do not invent an answer. Ask if a legal field is unclear.

name: Return an item you bought
description: Return or start a return for an item, with the reason and the proof the seller asks for.
l1c: Find the seller's return rule and the date you bought the item.
l1d: You can see whether a return is offered.
l2c: Ask for the return in the seller's channel, with the reason and the proof they list.
l2d: You can open a return.
l3c: Write what the seller said would happen next, or that they refused, and the date.
l3d: You can keep a record of the answer.
safety: Do not send a return to a payment link in an unexpected message. Use the seller's known channel.

name: Compare two routes
description: Compare two ways to get somewhere by time, changes, and cost.
l1c: Write two routes with their main steps.
l2c: Compare time, number of changes, and cost or effort, using figures you can point to.
l2d: You can compare on stated facts.
l3c: Choose one and name the fact that would make you switch.
l3d: You can choose and keep a switching condition.
safety: None.

name: Prepare papers for a trip
description: Gather the documents a specific trip requires and note one you still need to check.
l1c: From the carrier or the border page you are using, list the documents they name.
l1d: You can start from their list.
l2c: Set out the documents you have and mark each item on the list as present or missing.
l2d: You can match papers to a list.
l3c: Check one expiry or validity date and say whether it covers the travel dates.
l3d: You can check a date that matters.
safety: Use the official page for the trip. Do not rely on a memory of the rule. This skill does not give immigration advice.

name: Ask for directions and repeat them
description: Ask for directions and repeat them back so the person can correct you.
l1c: Ask for the way to a specific place, and let the person finish.
l2c: Repeat the steps in order and ask if you have them right.
l2d: You can play the directions back.
l3c: Write one landmark they gave you, and what you will do if you do not see it.
l3d: You can keep a landmark and a fallback.
safety: If you feel unsafe, end the conversation and use a public source instead.

name: Change a plan when transport fails
description: When a ride is cancelled or missed, choose the next way and tell a person who is waiting.
l1c: Write what failed and the time you noticed.
l2c: Choose the next available way from information you can show, and the new arrival time.
l2d: You can pick a replacement.
l3c: Tell the person who is meeting you the new time, and what you will do if that ride fails too.
l3d: You can update someone and keep a second fallback.
safety: Do not accept a ride from a stranger as the plan in this skill.

name: Keep a travel log
description: Keep a short log of where you went, what it cost, and one thing you would change.
l1c: Write the place, the main way you traveled, and one cost.
l2c: Add a second day and the total of the costs you wrote.
l2d: You can keep a running record.
l3c: Write one thing you would do differently on a similar day.
l3d: You can learn from the log.
safety: None.

name: Work out a time-zone gap
description: Convert a time in one place to the local time in another, and check it.
l1c: Write the two places and the local time you are converting.
l2c: Convert the time with a source you can show, including the date if it changes.
l2d: You can convert a time.
l3c: Propose a meeting time that is inside waking hours in both places, and show both local times.
l3d: You can use the conversion for a plan.
safety: Check the source on the day, because offsets change.

name: Find a book in a library catalog
description: Find a known book in a library catalog and then on the shelf or in the request system.
l1c: Search by title or author and open the record that matches the book you want.
l2c: Read the branch and the shelf mark, or the request button if it is not on the shelf.
l2d: You can tell where the book is.
l3c: Find it on the shelf or place a request, and say which you did.
l3d: You can turn a record into a book in your hands or on order.
safety: Use a library you are allowed to use.

name: Cite a source in a note
description: Attach a citation a reader could follow to a claim in your note.
l1c: Write a claim and the source you took it from, including the title.
l2c: Add the author, the date, and a page or a link the reader could use.
l2d: You can make a citation followable.
l3c: Mark which sentence is the source's and which is your summary.
l3d: You can tell a quotation from a summary.
safety: Do not invent a page or a link.

name: Skim a text for your question
description: Search a chapter for the answer to a question you wrote first.
l1c: Write the question before you start reading.
l1d: You can read with a question.
l2c: Find a heading or a paragraph that bears on the question, and mark it.
l2d: You can locate a relevant passage.
l3c: Answer the question from that passage, or write that the chapter does not answer it.
l3d: You can stop when the text does not answer.
safety: None.

name: Annotate a text
description: Mark a text with questions and definitions so you can reread only your marks.
l1c: Mark one sentence you do not understand and write the question beside it.
l2c: Look up one hard word and write a short meaning you will understand later.
l2d: You can leave a definition.
l3c: Read only your marks and say what the text is about, then check one point against the page.
l3d: You can use your annotation as a guide.
safety: Annotate only a copy you are allowed to mark.

name: Compare two accounts of one event
description: Read two accounts of the same event and list what they both say and where they differ.
l1c: Read two short accounts and write one sentence each says.
l2c: Write one point they share and one point they do not.
l2d: You can separate agreement from difference.
l3c: Name which difference you cannot settle from these two texts alone.
l3d: You can leave a conflict unresolved.
safety: Do not treat either account as proven just because it is printed.

name: Place an event on a timeline
description: Put an event on a timeline with what came before and after.
l1c: Write the event and a date or period you can point to in a source.
l1d: You can attach a time to an event.
l2c: Add one event before and one after, with their dates.
l2d: You can see sequence.
l3c: Say one way the earlier event makes the later one easier to understand, or say you see no link.
l3d: You can connect events or admit you cannot.
safety: Use a source for the dates. Do not invent a year.

name: Read a museum label
description: Read a museum label and separate what the object is from what the label claims about it.
l1c: From the label, say what the object is and where it is from.
l1d: You can read the basic facts.
l2c: Point to one sentence that interprets the object, not only names it.
l2d: You can see an interpretation.
l3c: Write a question the label does not answer.
l3d: You can leave a museum label with a question.
safety: Do not touch an object the museum says not to touch.

name: Run a simple home observation
description: Change one ordinary thing, watch what happens, and write the result without a grand claim.
l1c: Write what you will change and what you will watch, before you start.
l2c: Make the change, write what you saw, and keep a note of what you did not see.
l2d: You can record a result.
l3c: Write one sentence you will not claim, because you changed only one thing once.
l3d: You can keep the conclusion small.
safety: Use kitchen-safe materials such as water, food color, or a dropped object. No flames, no unknown chemicals, no electricity experiments.

name: Look up a word and use it
description: Look up an unfamiliar word and use it in a sentence that shows the meaning.
l1c: Look up a word in a dictionary you can name, and copy the meaning you will use.
l2c: Write a sentence of your own that would fail if the word meant something else.
l2d: You can use the word, not only define it.
l3c: If the dictionary gives another meaning, say why you did not use that one.
l3d: You can choose among meanings.
safety: None.

name: Play a game of chess
description: Play chess to checkmate or another agreed end, using a reference for any move you are unsure of.
l1c: Set up the pieces from a diagram and say which side moves first.
l1d: You can start a legal game.
l2c: Play until checkmate, stalemate, resignation, or an agreed draw, and name which ending it was.
l2d: You can finish a game.
l3c: Point to one of your moves that left a piece open, and say what you could have done instead.
l3d: You can learn from a position you reached.
safety: Use a reference for the rules. Do not treat this as a coaching certificate. Xiangqi is a different skill.

name: Play a game of Go
description: Play Go on a small board, capture or surround, and count the result with a reference.
l1c: Play on a small board with the liberty rule in front of you, and show one capture or say why there was none.
l1d: You can play by the capture rule.
l2c: Play until both players pass, and point to one group that lived or died.
l2d: You can reach the end of a small game.
l3c: Count the result with a reference or a stronger player, and say one point you would have played differently.
l3d: You can face a result.
safety: Rules differ by ruleset. Name the ruleset you used. This is not a ranking.

name: Play draughts
description: Play draughts or checkers to a finish, including one promotion if the game reaches it.
l1c: Play several moves that obey the direction and the capture rule you are using.
l2c: When a capture is available, take it if your rules require it, and show the position after.
l2d: You can follow the capture rule.
l3c: Play to a win, a loss, or a position you both agree is drawn, and name one move you would change.
l3d: You can finish and review.
safety: Say whether you are playing forced capture. Rules vary.

name: Play a trick-taking card game
description: Play a trick-taking game by following suit, and say who won a trick.
l1c: Play a hand in which you follow suit when you can, using the rules of one named game.
l2c: Point to a trick and say which card won it under those rules.
l2d: You can read a trick.
l3c: Before you play one card, say what you hope it will do, then say whether it did.
l3d: You can intend a card and see the result.
safety: Agree the game and the stakes before you start. Do not play for money you cannot lose.

name: Play a game of dominoes
description: Play a matching domino game to an empty hand or a blocked board.
l1c: Play tiles that match the open ends, using one named ruleset.
l2c: Show either a score you recorded or a board where nobody can play.
l2d: You can recognize an end condition.
l3c: Point to a tile you played and one you wish you had saved.
l3d: You can review a choice.
safety: Name the ruleset, because scoring differs.

name: Play mancala
description: Play a mancala game by sowing seeds and say how a turn ends.
l1c: Sow the seeds from one pit in the direction your rules use.
l2c: Play a turn that ends in a capture or an extra turn if the rules give one, and say which happened.
l2d: You can apply an end-of-turn rule.
l3c: Play until the rules say the game is over, and count the stores with the other player.
l3d: You can reach a counted result.
safety: Name the variant. Do not assume every mancala game captures the same way.

name: Solve a logic grid
description: Solve a logic grid by marking what is impossible, not by guessing.
l1c: Read one clue and mark the cells it makes true or false.
l2c: Use a mark you already made to cross out another cell, and say which mark allowed it.
l2d: You can chain a deduction.
l3c: Fill the answer only where every alternative is crossed out, and test it against each clue.
l3d: You can finish without a leftover contradiction.
safety: None.

name: Solve a cube and explain one step
description: Solve a 3x3 cube with a method you can explain, not by speed.
l1c: Complete one stage of a written method, such as a cross or a first layer, and show it.
l2c: Perform one sequence and say what it is for, in ordinary words.
l2d: You can explain a move, not only do it.
l3c: Solve the cube, and if you slip, return to the last stage you can recognize rather than starting in a panic.
l3d: You can recover a stage.
safety: Use a written method you may keep. Speed is not the criterion.

name: Recite a short text from memory
description: Learn a short text and recite it, then repair the line you miss.
l1c: Recite a short stanza or paragraph without the page.
l1d: You can hold a short text.
l2c: If you stop, take only the first word as a prompt and finish the line yourself.
l2d: You can recover from a small prompt.
l3c: Recite the whole text to a person, mark the line you missed, and say how you will practice that line.
l3d: You can perform and target the weak line.
safety: Choose a text you are allowed to perform. This is not a timed memory stunt.

name: Learn the names of people you meet
description: Learn and use the names of people you just met.
l1c: Repeat a person's name when they say it, and ask if you said it right.
l1d: You can check a name at once.
l2c: Use the name once later in the conversation, naturally.
l2d: You can recall a name in the moment.
l3c: If you forget, ask again, use the name, and write a respectful note to yourself if you need one.
l3d: You can recover a name without pretending.
safety: Use the name and pronouns the person gives you. Do not record people without asking.

name: Officiate a casual game
description: Apply agreed rules in a casual game and explain one call.
l1c: Before play, state the rule you will watch and how a point starts.
l1d: You can set the rule in advance.
l2c: Make one call during play and say the fact you saw.
l2d: You can call what you saw.
l3c: Hear one objection, keep or change the call, and say why.
l3d: You can respond to a dispute.
safety: Stop play for an injury. You are not a medical helper in this skill.

name: Set up a safe playing space
description: Set up a space for a game so the boundaries and the hazards are clear.
l1c: Mark the playing area and a place for bags and water.
l2c: Move one object that people could trip on, or move the game away from it.
l2d: You can reduce a trip hazard.
l3c: Tell the group the boundary and what happens if a ball leaves it.
l3d: You can brief the space.
safety: Do not play near traffic. Stop if the surface is unsafe.

name: Give credit for an idea
description: When you use someone's idea, say whose it was.
l1c: In a note or a meeting, attribute one idea to the person who offered it.
l2c: Say what you added, so the original idea stays visible.
l2d: You can tell their part from yours.
l3c: If you forgot someone, correct the record where the first version went.
l3d: You can repair a missing credit.
safety: Do not attribute a private comment the person did not want shared.

name: Divide work in a small group
description: Split a task so each person knows their part and how the parts meet.
l1c: Write the parts of a small task and who takes each one.
l2c: For one part, write what finished looks like and when it is needed.
l2d: You can make an assignment checkable.
l3c: Put the parts together and name one gap between them.
l3d: You can see the seam between people's work.
safety: Do not assign a dangerous task.

name: Welcome a new person
description: Help a new person take a first useful step in a group you already know.
l1c: Greet the person, say your name, and show them where to start.
l2c: Tell them one norm that would embarrass them if they learned it late.
l2d: You can share a norm in time.
l3c: Introduce them to one person relevant to why they came, and step back.
l3d: You can connect a newcomer and leave.
safety: Do not share other people's private information as orientation.

name: Ask for help specifically
description: Ask for a specific kind of help, from a person who can give it, by a time.
l1c: Write what you need, in a form another person could do.
l1d: You can make a concrete ask.
l2c: Ask someone who can actually help, and include a time.
l2d: You can direct the ask.
l3c: Record whether they agreed, refused, or offered a smaller help, and thank them.
l3d: You can accept the answer you got.
safety: A no is a complete answer.

name: Offer help that can be refused
description: Offer help in a way the other person can decline without awkwardness.
l1c: Offer a specific action, not a general 'let me know'.
l1d: You can make a concrete offer.
l2c: Ask in a way that allows no, and stop if they decline.
l2d: You can hear a refusal.
l3c: If they accept, do the action you offered and check it matched what they wanted.
l3d: You can deliver the help you named.
safety: Do not help in a way that takes over a task they wanted to keep.

name: Track a small project
description: Track a small project with a next action, a waiting item, and a done item.
l1c: Write three columns or a list with at least one next action.
l2c: When something changes, move it and write the date.
l2d: You can keep the tracker current.
l3c: For an item that is waiting, write who it is waiting on, and send or make the request.
l3d: You can act on a blocker.
safety: None.

name: Write a handover note
description: Leave a note so another person can continue a task without asking you the basics.
l1c: Write what is done and what is not.
l1d: You can say where the work stands.
l2c: Write the next action and where the files or objects are.
l2d: You can point to the next step.
l3c: Write one thing that will go wrong if the next person does not know it.
l3d: You can warn about a real risk.
safety: Leave out passwords. Do not include private data the next person does not need.

name: Negotiate a deadline
description: Ask for a deadline you can meet, and leave with a date both sides share.
l1c: Before you accept a date, say what the work includes.
l2c: Propose a date and the reason it is realistic.
l2d: You can ask for a date on purpose.
l3c: Restate the agreed date and what will be ready, in a message both sides have.
l3d: You can lock the agreement in writing.
safety: Do not promise a date you already know you will miss.

name: Cancel an unwanted subscription
description: Find a subscription you did not mean to keep and cancel it through the service's own path.
l1c: Point to a repeating charge on a statement and the name of the service.
l2c: Open the cancellation path on the service you already use, not a link from an unexpected message.
l2d: You can start from the real service.
l3c: Save the confirmation or the end date, and say what you will check on the next statement.
l3d: You can prove a cancellation is in progress.
safety: Do not give a card number to a helper site. Do not pay a fee to a third party to cancel.

name: Read a payslip or an invoice
description: Read a payslip or an invoice so you can point to the gross amount, a deduction or tax line, and the amount paid.
l1c: Point to the gross amount and the amount that was paid or is due.
l1d: You can find the two totals.
l2c: Explain one deduction, tax, or fee in ordinary words.
l2d: You can read a line between the totals.
l3c: Mark one figure you do not understand and write the question you would ask the payer.
l3d: You can turn confusion into a question.
