safety: This is not tax advice. Hide the document's identifiers if you show the skill to someone else.

name: Say what could stop a plan
description: Name a way a small plan could fail, and change one step because of it.
l1c: Write a small plan in three steps.
l2c: Write one likely way it fails, based on a fact you can point to.
l2d: You can see a real threat to the plan.
l3c: Change one step to reduce that failure, and say what you did not try to prevent.
l3d: You can adjust a plan and leave a residual risk.
safety: This is not a safety case for a dangerous activity.

name: Check a home before you leave
description: Walk a short checklist before you leave home, and fix one thing the list catches.
l1c: Write the checks that matter for your home, such as the cooker, the taps, the windows, and the lock.
l1d: You can make a leaving list.
l2c: Walk the list and tick only what you looked at.
l2d: You can do the checks.
l3c: Find one item that was not ready, fix it or decide to stay, and say which.
l3d: You can let the list change what you do.
safety: If you smell gas or see smoke, leave and contact the local emergency number. Do not investigate a gas smell.

name: Squat with control
description: Squat down and stand up with a stable foot position, and stop if pain is sharp.
l1c: Squat to a depth you can stand up from, with both feet staying quiet on the floor.
l2c: Ask a person or use a side-on recording to name one fault, such as heels lifting, and repeat with that fault reduced.
l2d: You can correct a fault you can see.
l3c: Do a few repetitions and stop when form breaks or when you feel sharp pain, and say which stop you used.
l3d: You can stop on form, not on a number.
safety: Sharp pain means stop. This is not a medical exercise plan. Use a support if you need one.

name: Hold a plank with form
description: Hold a plank position and come down when the form goes, not when a clock says so.
l1c: Set a plank on hands or forearms and show a line from head to heels that a helper can see.
l2c: Hold only while the line stays, then come down and say what started to sag.
l2d: You can end on form.
l3c: Repeat from the knees or from the toes, choosing the version where you can keep the line, and say why.
l3d: You can choose a version you can do well.
safety: Stop for sharp pain. Do not hold your breath. This is not a timed fitness test.

name: Move through a short sequence
description: Learn a short sequence of movements and repeat it without the demonstration in front of you.
l1c: Follow a short sequence from a teacher or a video you are allowed to use.
l2c: Do the sequence without watching, and name the move you forgot.
l2d: You can hold the order.
l3c: Repeat it and keep one point of form, such as a steady breath or a soft knee, and say when you lost it.
l3d: You can add quality to memory.
safety: Stay inside a range that does not cause sharp pain. This is not a yoga qualification.

name: Juggle three balls
description: Juggle three balls in a cascade and pick up after a drop.
l1c: Throw one ball from hand to hand so it peaks at a height you can catch.
l1d: You can throw one ball on purpose.
l2c: Start a cascade and complete several catches, or stop and say which throw collapsed.
l2d: You can begin a three-ball pattern.
l3c: After a drop, restart from the same start position without changing the pattern in a panic, and say what you reset.
l3d: You can restart cleanly.
safety: Use soft balls in an open space. Do not juggle hard objects.

name: Stretch and stop before pain
description: Stretch a muscle you can name and stop at strong tension rather than pain.
l1c: Move into a stretch for a muscle you can name, and point to where you feel it.
l2c: Hold only while the feeling is tension, and come out when it becomes pain or when you cannot breathe easily.
l2d: You can tell tension from pain.
l3c: Stretch the other side and say which side felt tighter, without forcing them to match.
l3d: You can notice a difference and not force it.
safety: Sharp pain means stop. Do not bounce. This is not a flexibility program or a treatment.

name: Notice effort and ease off
description: During ordinary exercise you already do, notice when effort rises and take an easier step.
l1c: During a walk, a ride, or another familiar effort, say whether it is easy, steady, or hard.
l2c: When it becomes hard, slow down or stop, and say what you changed.
l2d: You can reduce effort on purpose.
l3c: Either continue at the easier pace or end the session, and say which you chose and why.
l3d: You can decide the rest of the session.
safety: Stop and seek help for chest pain, fainting, or distress. This skill is not a diagnosis and not a training plan.

name: Host a simple meal
description: Host a simple meal where a guest knows when to arrive and what they are eating.
l1c: Invite a guest with a time and one sentence about the food.
l1d: You can make a clear invitation.
l2c: Have the meal ready enough to sit down with the guest, and offer water.
l2d: You can serve a simple meal.
l3c: Ask about a food limit before you cook, and change or label one dish because of the answer.
l3d: You can adapt a meal to a guest.
safety: Ask about allergies. Do not guess.

name: Blot a fresh stain
description: Blot a fresh wet stain with water and stop before you add a chemical.
l1c: Blot a fresh wet stain with a clean cloth and water, lifting rather than scrubbing.
l1d: You can blot a fresh stain.
l2c: Look at the cloth and say whether the stain is lighter, and stop if it is spreading.
l2d: You can tell if blotting is helping.
l3c: If a mark remains, say you will read a care label or ask before using any cleaner, and do not invent one.
l3d: You can stop at the edge of what water can do.
safety: Do not mix cleaners. Do not use a solvent in this skill.

name: Write a packing list for someone else
description: Write a packing list another person can use for a trip you both understand.
l1c: Ask the destination, the length, and one activity before you write the list.
l1d: You can start from their trip.
l2c: Write items a person could pack, grouped, without brand names they do not need.
l2d: You can write a usable list.
l3c: Hear one item they refuse, take it off or say why you would keep it, and agree the list.
l3d: You can revise a list with the traveler.
safety: Do not pack medicines for another person.

name: Explain a rule of a game
description: Explain one rule of a game so a new player can apply it on the next turn.
l1c: Explain one rule without reading, using the pieces or cards.
l2c: Play one example of the rule and one example of a break.
l2d: You can show the boundary of the rule.
l3c: Let the new player use the rule, and correct only if they break it.
l3d: You can tell teaching from playing their turn.
safety: None.

name: Keep a score others can check
description: Keep a score that another player can reconstruct from your marks.
l1c: Record one score change so a player can see who gained it.
l1d: You can write a point down.
l2c: Update the total after each change and show the arithmetic once.
l2d: You can keep a running score.
l3c: When someone doubts a total, show the marks that add up to it, or correct it.
l3d: You can defend or fix a score.
safety: Agree the scoring rule before you start.

name: Tune a string to a reference
description: Tune one string of an instrument to a reference note, and say when it is close.
l1c: Play a reference note and the string, and say whether the string is lower or higher.
l2c: Turn the tuner the right way and stop when a tuner or a listener says it matches.
l2d: You can tune one string.
l3c: Compare that string with the next string by the method your instrument uses, and say whether the pair agrees.
l3d: You can check one interval, not a full setup.
safety: Do not force a peg. Stop if a string might break. This is one string, not instrument repair.

name: Lead a group clap
description: Start a clap and bring a small group in with you.
l1c: Clap a tempo and count the group in.
l2c: Keep the clap going while the group joins, and nod or speak if they rush.
l2d: You can hold a group tempo.
l3c: Give a clear ending and stop with the group, then say whether they finished together.
l3d: You can end a group sound.
safety: Keep volume comfortable.

name: Draw a rough floor plan
description: Draw the outline of a room and the doors, good enough to plan where a table goes.
l1c: Draw the walls and mark the door.
l2c: Add the large furniture in places that match the room, and check by looking.
l2d: You can place objects in the sketch.
l3c: Draw one piece in a new place and say whether the door still opens.
l3d: You can use the sketch to test an idea.
safety: This is a rough plan, not a measured technical drawing for building work.

name: Arrange a small display
description: Arrange a few objects so a viewer can tell which one is the focus.
l1c: Place one object as the focus and say why the eye should go there.
l2c: Add two other objects that do not steal the focus, and ask a viewer where they looked first.
l2d: You can support a focus.
l3c: Move or remove the object that stole attention, and show the difference.
l3d: You can edit an arrangement.
safety: Do not use a candle or a heat source as part of the display in this skill.

name: Write a recipe card someone can cook
description: Write a recipe from a dish you made so another person could cook it.
l1c: Write the ingredients you used and the steps in order.
l2c: Add one check the cook can taste or see, such as 'until the onion is soft'.
l2d: You can give the cook a sign.
l3c: Ask someone to read it and add the step they say is missing.
l3d: You can repair a recipe from a reader.
safety: Include allergen ingredients by name. Do not invent a food-safety time.

name: Taste and adjust a pan sauce
description: After browning, make a simple pan sauce and adjust salt or acidity.
l1c: After cooking, add a liquid you can name and scrape the browned bits into it.
l1d: You can start a pan sauce.
l2c: Let it thicken slightly, taste, and say what it needs.
l2d: You can judge a sauce.
l3c: Add salt, a sour drop, or a little more liquid, and say which way the taste moved.
l3d: You can steer a sauce one step.
safety: Mind the steam. This is not a stock-making skill and not a lesson in flambé.

name: Set a table for a meal
description: Set a table so each person has what the meal requires.
l1c: Set a place with a plate, a glass, and the tool the meal needs.
l2c: Set every place the same way, with a clear path to sit.
l2d: You can set a table for a group.
l3c: Add or remove a tool because of the menu, and say why.
l3d: You can set a table for the food, not from habit.
safety: Knives stay at the place setting, not in a walkway.

name: Label a leftover
description: Put a leftover in a container with a name and a date, and say you are not deciding a medical storage rule.
l1c: Put leftover food in a clean container and close it.
l2c: Write what it is and the date you packed it.
l2d: You can label a leftover.
l3c: Later, read the label and either use it if it still looks and smells as it did, or discard it if you are unsure.
l3d: You can use a label to make a cautious choice.
safety: When unsure, discard the food. Do not taste to test safety. Do not invent a safe number of days.

name: Read a timetable
description: Read a public timetable and pick a departure that gets you there before a deadline.
l1c: Point to the destination and the list of times on a timetable.
l1d: You can read the frame of a timetable.
l2c: Choose a departure that arrives before a time you wrote down, and show the arrival.
l2d: You can pick a service.
l3c: Say what you will do if that service is late or cancelled.
l3d: You can pair a choice with a fallback.
safety: Check the date on the timetable. Holiday services differ.

name: Learn a route in a building
description: Learn the way from an entrance to a room, and back, without the signs if they fail.
l1c: Walk from the entrance to the room and name two landmarks.
l2c: Walk back and say the landmarks in reverse.
l2d: You can reverse a route.
l3c: Say how you would leave if your usual corridor were closed.
l3d: You can name a second way out.
safety: Follow the building's fire exit signs in an alarm. This practice is for ordinary wayfinding, not an evacuation drill you invent.

name: Introduce yourself in a minute
description: Introduce yourself for a specific room, with your name and why you are there.
l1c: Say your name and why you are in the room, in a few sentences.
l1d: You can open with the point.
l2c: Take out a detail that does not matter for this room, and say it again.
l2d: You can tailor an introduction.
l3c: End with one way the listener can respond, such as a question they could ask.
l3d: You can leave the other person a way in.
safety: You choose how much personal detail to give.

name: Paraphrase a paragraph
description: Rewrite a paragraph in your own words without losing the claim.
l1c: Underline the sentence that carries the claim.
l2c: Rewrite the paragraph without copying a sentence, and keep the claim.
l2d: You can paraphrase.
l3c: Compare the two and restore one fact you dropped.
l3d: You can see what a paraphrase lost.
safety: Mark the source. Do not present the paraphrase as the source's wording.

name: Take a phone message
description: Take a message for someone else with the name, the ask, and the callback.
l1c: Write who called and what they want.
l2c: Read the number or the reply path back to the caller.
l2d: You can check the reply path.
l3c: Give the message to the right person and say how urgent the caller said it was.
l3d: You can deliver a message intact.
safety: Do not write a password or a payment number in the message.

name: Make a quiet-hours agreement
description: Agree quiet hours with someone you live with, in words you can both check.
l1c: Propose a start and an end, and the rooms they cover.
l2c: Change one part because of what the other person needs, and restate the whole agreement.
l2d: You can revise a house rule together.
l3c: On a day it applies, follow it or say you broke it, and agree how you will handle the next time.
l3d: You can live with a rule you wrote.
safety: An agreement is not a way to control another person. Either person can reopen it.

name: Sort a wash before you start
description: Sort dirty clothes into loads the labels allow, before any machine starts.
l1c: Separate clothes into at least two piles using color or the care label.
l2c: Remove one item that does not belong, and say which symbol or risk made you do it.
l2d: You can exclude a mismatch.
l3c: Choose which pile to wash first and why, such as what you need tomorrow.
l3d: You can sequence loads.
safety: Follow care labels. Do not add bleach unless a label you are reading allows it.

name: Thread a needle and finish the thread
description: Thread a needle and fasten the thread so a stitch will not pull straight out.
l1c: Thread a needle and pull enough thread to sew a short line.
l2c: Knot or fasten the end and show that a gentle pull does not undo it.
l2d: You can secure the thread.
l3c: Sew a few stitches in scrap cloth and fasten the other end.
l3d: You can start and stop a line of stitches.
safety: Keep the point away from other people. This supports mending; it is not a separate garment-making skill.

name: Read the scale of a map
description: Use a map scale to say whether a distance is a short walk or a long one.
l1c: Point to the scale bar or the ratio on a map.
l2c: Measure one route on the map and convert it with the scale.
l2d: You can turn the scale into a distance.
l3c: Say whether that distance is a casual walk for you, and what would make the judgement wrong, such as hills the scale does not show.
l3d: You can use a distance without forgetting what the scale omits.
safety: Scale is not terrain. Do not plan a remote route from scale alone.

name: Spot a contradiction in your notes
description: Find two notes that disagree and decide which one you will check.
l1c: Point to two of your notes that cannot both be true.
l2c: Write which source or page you will open to settle it.
l2d: You can aim a check.
l3c: After checking, strike or rewrite the note that was wrong, and leave the date of the correction.
l3d: You can repair a note.
safety: None.

name: Practice an explanation out loud
description: Practice a short explanation aloud and fix the sentence where you stumble.
l1c: Explain a topic aloud for a minute without reading.
l2c: Note the sentence where you stopped or circled, in a few words.
l2d: You can find the weak sentence.
l3c: Rewrite that sentence and say the explanation again, including the new line.
l3d: You can improve a spoken explanation.
safety: Do not present the practice as a checked fact.

name: Build a checklist from a miss
description: After something goes wrong, write a checklist that would have caught it.
l1c: Write what went wrong in one sentence.
l2c: Write the check that would have shown the problem before it happened.
l2d: You can turn a miss into a check.
l3c: Use the checklist on the next similar task and tick the new item.
l3d: You can apply a checklist born from a miss.
safety: Do not write a checklist for a dangerous trade you are not trained for.

name: Choose a gift for a person
description: Choose a gift from what you know about a person, and say what you are not assuming.
l1c: Write one interest or need you have actually seen or been told.
l2c: Choose a gift that matches that fact, within a budget you wrote down.
l2d: You can match a gift to a fact and a budget.
l3c: Name one assumption you will not use, such as age or gender, and show the gift does not depend on it.
l3d: You can avoid a lazy assumption.
safety: Do not buy for a person from a private fact they did not share with you.

name: Pack a meal to eat later
description: Pack a meal that is still edible when you eat it, and say what you kept cold.
l1c: Choose foods that can sit until you will eat them, and leave out one that cannot.
l1d: You can choose food for later.
l2c: Pack it so it does not leak, and keep the cold item cold if it needs cold.
l2d: You can pack a portable meal.
l3c: Eat it at the planned time and write one change for next time.
l3d: You can learn from the packed meal.
safety: When unsure whether a food needed cold, do not eat it. Do not invent a safe number of hours.

name: Read a recipe before you start
description: Read a recipe through, set out the ingredients, and notice a missing item before you cook.
l1c: Read the recipe once before you turn on the heat.
l1d: You can read before you cook.
l2c: Set out every ingredient the recipe names, or mark the one you do not have.
l2d: You can discover a gap before cooking.
l3c: Either substitute an ingredient you can justify or choose not to start, and say which.
l3d: You can stop or adapt before the heat is on.
safety: Do not substitute an allergen. Do not start a deep-fry you have not planned.
